vocabulary.definition: To see if a number is bigger, smaller, or equal to another.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ver si un número es mayor, menor o igual que otro.
vocabulary.visual: -3 < 2 because -3 is farther left on the number line than 2

examples.why: It judges one value against another.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange numbers by size, from least to greatest or greatest to least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Acomodar números por tamaño, de menor a mayor o de mayor a menor.
vocabulary.visual: Least to greatest: -5, -2, 0, 3, 7 (left to right on the number line)
vocabulary.cloze: To arrange numbers from least to greatest or greatest to least is to ___ them.

examples.why: The values are arranged by size.
No arrangement by size has happened.

vocabulary.definition: The > sign, showing one number is bigger.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo >, que muestra que un número es mayor.
vocabulary.visual: 4 > -1 because 4 is to the right of -1 on the number line
vocabulary.cloze: On a number line, a number farther to the right is ___ another number.

examples.why: -3 is farther right on the line, so it is greater.
-8 is farther left, which makes it the smaller value.

vocabulary.definition: The < sign, showing one number is smaller.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo <, que muestra que un número es menor.
vocabulary.visual: -6 < -2 because -6 is farther left — it is farther from zero
vocabulary.cloze: On a number line, a number farther to the left is ___ another number.

examples.why: -15 sits farther left, so it is the lesser value.
-20 is deeper still, so this reverses the order.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number smaller than zero, like -5.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero menor que cero, como -5.
vocabulary.visual: -4 is 4 units to the LEFT of zero on the number line
vocabulary.cloze: An integer less than zero, like −6, is a ___.

examples.why: It is an integer less than zero.
It is greater than zero, so it is positive.

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números enteros y sus opuestos, como -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A whole number or its opposite is an ___.

examples.why: Whole numbers, their opposites, and zero.
A number between two whole numbers is not an integer.

copyPanel.formula: Left is Less (<) | Right is Greater (>)
steps: 1. Plot or visualize numbers on a horizontal number line
2. Numbers further to the left are always less than numbers to the right
3. For negatives: A negative number with a larger absolute value is smaller (-10 < -2)

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: A Game of Golf
revealWordProblem.text: Golf scores are measured as strokes over or under par. Par is the number of golf strokes considered necessary to get the ball in the hole, so a score under par is written as a negative integer and a score over par is written as a positive integer. The scorecard shows six players' scores relative to par after seven holes of a 9-hole round (par = 35): Evelyn -2, Brielle +1, Terrance 0, Reginald -3, Sofia +4, Francisco +2. Order the six scores from least to greatest to rank the players from first place (the current leader) to last place. Who is winning after 7 holes, and who has the most strokes to make up?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A golf score card with par equal to 35, showing six players' scores and how far each is over or under par.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: From least to greatest, the scores are -3, -2, 0, +1, +2, +4, which ranks the players Reginald, Evelyn, Terrance, Brielle, Francisco, Sofia. Reginald is winning after 7 holes because -3 is the least score — it is farthest left on the number line, meaning he used the fewest strokes compared to par. Sofia is in last place because +4 is the greatest score, farthest right on the number line, meaning she has used the most strokes over par.

reviewCheck.stem: Three cities have temperatures of -12°F, -5°F, and 3°F. Which city is warmest?
reviewCheck.explanation: 3°F is the greatest because it is farthest to the right on the number line. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, 3.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, ___.
This one is farthest to the left on the number line, which makes it the coldest reading rather than the warmest. Warmer temperatures sit farther right.
The three readings are different numbers, so they cannot describe the same temperature. Place them on a number line and compare their positions.
hints: Warmest = greatest temperature. On a thermometer, greater is higher — farther right on a number line.
Compare positions on a number line: temperatures farther right are warmer. Check where negatives sit versus positives.
Place -12, -5, and 3 on a number line and find the one farthest to the right. That city is warmest.
reviewCheck.stemEs: Tres ciudades tienen temperaturas de -12°F, -5°F y 3°F. ¿Cuál ciudad es la más cálida?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: 3°F es la mayor porque está más a la derecha en la recta numérica. El orden del más frío al más cálido es -12, -5, 3.
hintsEs: El más cálido = la temperatura mayor. En un termómetro, mayor es más alto, o sea más a la derecha en una recta numérica.
Compara posiciones en una recta numérica: las temperaturas más a la derecha son más cálidas. Revisa dónde quedan los negativos frente a los positivos.
Coloca −12, −5 y 3 en una recta numérica y halla el más a la derecha. Esa ciudad es la más cálida.
